entries.regs_verbatim: It is unlawful to angle with a fishing line to which more than one artificial fly is attached (i.e., to use dropper flies). It is unlawful to fish with nets, including dip nets, minnow nets, gill nets or cast nets. entries.regs_verbatim: The classified waters of B.C. are highly productive trout streams. These streams are classified as either Class I or Class II and are listed in the Water-Specific Tables for each Region. Anglers are required to hold a basic angling licence and a Classified Waters Licence when fishing on a stream during the period when it is classified. A Steelhead Conservation Surcharge Stamp is required at all times when fishing for steelhead, or when fishing classified waters during the period when steelhead are known to be present. If you are a B.C. resident, your Classified Waters Licence permits you to angle in all classified waters throughout the licence year. If you are a NON-GUIDED or GUIDED Non-Resident or Non-Resident Alien, your Classified Waters Licence is sold on a per day basis and is date and water-specific, and each licence may not exceed 8 consecutive days. A first-come-first-serve booking system is in place for these Kootenay Class II waters: Michel Creek, Skookumchuck Creek, and the Wigwam River. EXCEPTION: Non-Resident Aliens (whether GUIDED or NON-GUIDED) may only purchase one Classified Waters Licence for the Dean River per licence year.

entries.regs_verbatim: If you are 16 years of age or older, you must have a valid basic licence to sport fish for any species of fish in non-tidal waters (including salmon). Basic and supplementary licences and stamps are not valid in National Parks. If you are under 16 and a resident of B.C., you may sport fish without any licence or stamp, you do not need to be accompanied by a licence holder, and you are entitled to your own quota of fish. If you are under 16 and not a resident of B.C., you do not require any licence or stamp to sport fish, but you must be accompanied by a person 16 years or older who holds the appropriate licences and stamps, and any fish you keep must be counted as part of the catch and possession of your accompanying licence holder. If you are an Indian and a resident of B.C., you are not required to obtain any type of fishing licence or stamp to sport fish in non-tidal waters. All Metis individuals intending to sport fish in non-tidal waters are required, under the Wildlife Act, to hold appropriate angling licences and stamps.
